# Analytic and Algebraic Methods

## Overview
Analytic and Algebraic Methods convert continuous geometric primitives into discrete volumetric grids by evaluating exact geometric intersections or integrals against voxel cells [S1, unofficial]. This approach samples analytical implicit surfaces into a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md) for [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
Not given in the sources.

## Subtopics

### [Signed Distance Field Voxelization](3849-signed-distance-field-voxelization.md)
Computes the signed Euclidean distance to the nearest surface point for every voxel. It differs from [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) by computing exact geometric distances rather than projected coverage, and from [SDF-based Binary Voxelization](2402-sdf-based-binary-voxelization.md) by retaining continuous distance values.

### [Surface-Aware Discretization](6820-surface-aware-discretization.md)
Computes the effective volume of each voxel based on the intersection with the target mesh using [Monte Carlo ray tracing](#1940-monte-carlo-method-for-multiple-scattering.md). It differs from standard binary [voxelization](#12-voxelization.md) by estimating fractional occupancy, and from analytic methods by relying on stochastic sampling rather than closed-form geometric intersections.

### [Analytic Voxelization](10493-analytic-voxelization.md)
Converts parametrically defined continuous geometric objects into digital object representations (voxels).

### Recursive Voxelization with Interval Arithmetic
Rendering of recursively voxelized object space with interval arithmetic was first proposed by [136] [S1, unofficial].

## Background
In rendering general-form implicit surfaces, one approach is to sample an analytical implicit into a regular grid by voxelization [119], followed by direct volume rendering [S1, unofficial]. Rendering of recursively voxelized object space with interval arithmetic was first proposed by [136] [S1, unofficial]. [Discrete ray tracing](#3020-discrete-ray-tracing.md) [140, 118] and GPU-based volume [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) are also valid approaches to rendering voxellized datasets [S1, unofficial].
